heard.hinweis: Körper am 2026-11-20 neu gebaut (Modalsynthese der Kreismembran mit mvmfilter-Resonatoren, drei verdrahtete Achsen pitched/strikepos/damping, tension entfernt). Die frühere Aufzeichnung — Status „nicht abgenommen“, BJ 2026-07-30: „drum-head: nicht autorisiert, strikepos habe ich nicht getestet“ — betraf den Vorgänger, dessen Code keine seiner erklärten Achsen las. Gate: die Bewegungsprüfung liest die Drift des Reibpunkts an allen 27 Ecken als Rauschvarianz, nicht als Bewegung (im Körper erklärt); die Lautheitsstreuung über die Ecken liegt je nach Rauschziehung bei 0,5 bis 1,2 dB (Grenze 1,0). 16 Stimmen kosten bei 176400 das Zwei- bis Vierfache des Vorgängers.

techniques.why: struck drum / timpani / tom: a circular membrane struck once and left to ring down, the played key always on the (1,1) mode that carries a drum's note. Modal synthesis: ten `mode` resonators on the Bessel modes, weighted by the mode shape at the strike radius, decays from measured T60s. `kettle` runs from a free ideal membrane (inharmonic, a tom-like thump) to the air-loaded head of a 64 cm timpano measured by Christian et al. (JASA 76, 1984): partials near 1:1.5:2, a real note. Not `drum_head` (the standing, rubbed skin), not a tabla (its loaded head is harmonic), no hand slap. Limits: it decays by itself, so a long ring needs a long release; every knob is read at the stroke; a struck note restarts the head, a legato note retunes the ring; from about 220 Hz up 2f and 3f outweigh the note within 0.3 s; (2,2) and (0,3) cross near kettle .34 and beat there.
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: mallet
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; A struck circular membrane by modal synthesis: ten Bessel modes of an ideal membrane,
; moved by `kettle` towards the air-loaded modes MEASURED on a 64 cm timpano (Christian et al.,
; JASA 76 (1984), as tabulated by Packer, Durham MSc 1993, Tables 7.1/7.2). The heard pitch
; of a kettledrum is the (1,1) mode (Rossing, Physics Today 45(3), 1992), so the played key IS
; (1,1) at every kettle position and nothing jumps when the knob moves.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kket    = 1.0    ; kettle[0.0..1.0]: free membrane to kettle-loaded head
kstr    = 0.75   ; strike[0.65..0.85]: where the head is struck, towards the rim
kslk    = 0.0    ; slack[0.0..0.21]: how far a hard stroke stretches the head
kmal    = 2.0    ; mallet[1.0..8.0]: contact corner as a multiple of the played pitch
; --- THE TEN MODES, (0,1) (1,1) (2,1) (0,2) (3,1) (1,2) (4,1) (2,2) (0,3) (5,1).
;     iJ: Bessel zeros j_mn. iM: the order m. iN: |J_m+1(j_mn)|, x sqrt2 for m = 0 (the
;     mode's norm). iRi: ideal ratio re (1,1) = j_mn / j_11. iRt: the timpano's measured ratio
;     re (1,1). iQ: pi f T60 / ln 1000 from the same drum's measured decays, held constant
;     across register and at both kettle ends ((0,1) and (0,3) are upper bounds: T60 < 0.3 s).
;     The (0,n) modes radiate best and die first; that is the membrane, not a damping knob.
iJ[]    fillarray 2.40483, 3.83171, 5.13562, 5.52008, 6.38016, 7.01559, 7.58834, 8.41724, 8.65373, 8.77148
iM[]    fillarray 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 1, 4, 2, 0, 5
iN[]    fillarray 0.73419, 0.40276, 0.33967, 0.48121, 0.29827, 0.30012, 0.26836, 0.27138, 0.38389, 0.24543
iRi[]   fillarray 0.6276, 1.0000, 1.3403, 1.4406, 1.6651, 1.8309, 1.9804, 2.1967, 2.2585, 2.2892
iRt[]   fillarray 0.81, 1.00, 1.50, 1.65, 1.97, 2.00, 2.44, 2.86, 2.71, 2.91
iQ[]    fillarray 19, 63, 199, 52, 417, 78, 325, 112, 64, 592
; --- ONE STRIKE = ONE REINIT. The whole bank, its exciter and every per-strike number live
;     between HIT and rireturn, so a strike starts the head from rest (a re-strike restarts
;     the ring) and the knobs are read at the moment of the stroke. i(k) reads 0 on the build
;     pass, hence the key guard; `kup` is still 0 there, so the build pass does not strike.
kup     timeinsts
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit HIT
        endif
HIT:
is      limit i(kstr), 0.65, 0.85
im      limit i(kmal), 1.0, 8.0
ik      limit i(kket), 0.0, 1.0
id      limit i(kslk), 0.0, 0.21
iv      limit i(kvel), 0.05, 1.0
ikc     = i(kc)
ikc     = (ikc < 20 ? 220 : ikc)
igl     = sqrt(1 + id * iv * iv)               ; the stretch at the stroke (kg at knote 0)
; --- THE MALLET: a one-pole stand-in for the Hertz contact, its corner a multiple of the KEY
;     (contact time grows with the struck mass, Doutaut & Chaigne 1994; the proportion is
;     this entry's own). A fixed-Hz corner would tilt the bank across the keyboard.
ifc     limit ikc * im, 20, 8000
; A key change WITHOUT a stroke (legato, bind) retunes the ringing head: the key glides in
; log over 5 ms, restarted at each stroke, and kvl below follows it, so the ring keeps its level.
klc     portk log(kc), 0.005, log(ikc)
kcs     = exp(klc)
iamp    = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1 : 0)
acon    mpulse iamp, 0
aex     tone acon, ifc
; --- PER MODE, at the stroke: ratio, strike weight, normalisation term, decay time.
;     Ratio: ideal * (timpano / ideal) ^ kettle, a log interpolation that is this entry's own.
;     Weight: |J_m(j_mn * r/a)| / norm, by a 30-term power series. Signs are dropped and the
;     observation is flat (no listening point): declared, not physics.
;     Normalisation is L1 over what the mallet passes, so the attack holds across mallet,
;     strike and register; a mode outside 20 Hz..16 kHz neither sounds nor counts.
ir[]    init 10
iw[]    init 10
ib[]    init 10
itau[]  init 10
isum    = 0
iesum   = 0
ii      = 0
while ii < 10 do
  ir[ii] = iRi[ii] * (iRt[ii] / iRi[ii]) ^ ik
  ih     = iJ[ii] * is / 2
  it     = 1
  ic     = 1
  while ic <= iM[ii] do
    it   = it * ih / ic
    ic   += 1
  od
  ij     = it
  iq     = 1
  while iq < 30 do
    it   = -it * ih * ih / (iq * (iq + iM[ii]))
    ij   += it
    iq   += 1
  od
  iw[ii] = abs(ij) / iN[ii]
  ifq    = ikc * ir[ii] * igl
  ib[ii] = (ifq > 20 && ifq < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
  isum   += iw[ii] * ib[ii] / sqrt(1 + (ifq / ifc) ^ 2)
  iesum  += iw[ii] * iw[ii]
  itau[ii] = iQ[ii] / ($M_PI * ikc * ir[ii])
  ii     += 1
od
; G = 3.52 is a LEVEL choice: one stroke at the defaults, 220 Hz, peaks near asig 1.6.
; isum is 0 only when no mode is in the band; then nothing sounds and inrm must stay finite.
inrm    = 3.52 / (isum > 0 ? isum : 1)
; --- SLACK: a hard stroke stretches the head, tension follows the membrane's energy and so
;     the pitch falls back as the ring decays (energy law: Marogna, Avanzini & Bank, DAFx-10).
;     At slack 0.21 and full velocity that is the 10 % of a bass drum (Rossing 1992).
kE      = 0
kk      = 0
while kk < 10 do
  kE    += iw[kk] * iw[kk] * exp(-2 * knote / itau[kk])
  kk    += 1
od
kg      = sqrt(1 + id * iv * iv * kE / iesum)
kq0     = kcs * ir[0] * kg
kp0     limit kq0, 20, 16000
a0      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp0 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp0 / sr), iQ[0]
kq1     = kcs * ir[1] * kg
kp1     limit kq1, 20, 16000
a1      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp1 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp1 / sr), iQ[1]
kq2     = kcs * ir[2] * kg
kp2     limit kq2, 20, 16000
a2      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp2 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp2 / sr), iQ[2]
kq3     = kcs * ir[3] * kg
kp3     limit kq3, 20, 16000
a3      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp3 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp3 / sr), iQ[3]
kq4     = kcs * ir[4] * kg
kp4     limit kq4, 20, 16000
a4      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp4 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp4 / sr), iQ[4]
kq5     = kcs * ir[5] * kg
kp5     limit kq5, 20, 16000
a5      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp5 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp5 / sr), iQ[5]
kq6     = kcs * ir[6] * kg
kp6     limit kq6, 20, 16000
a6      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp6 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp6 / sr), iQ[6]
kq7     = kcs * ir[7] * kg
kp7     limit kq7, 20, 16000
a7      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp7 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp7 / sr), iQ[7]
kq8     = kcs * ir[8] * kg
kp8     limit kq8, 20, 16000
a8      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp8 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp8 / sr), iQ[8]
kq9     = kcs * ir[9] * kg
kp9     limit kq9, 20, 16000
a9      mode aex * cos($M_PI * kp9 / sr), (sr / $M_PI) * sin($M_PI * kp9 / sr), iQ[9]
; mode is bilinear: pre-warp each frequency and scale its input by cos(pi f / sr), so a
; mode rings at the same pitch and level at 44.1 and at 176.4 kHz.
; A mode that leaves 20 Hz..16 kHz mid-ring (slack, a legato key change) fades over 4 ms
; instead of switching; ib[] is its state at the stroke.
kg0     = (kq0 > 20 && kq0 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb0     portk kg0, 0.004, ib[0]
ab0     interp kb0, 0, 0, ib[0]
asum    = a0 * iw[0] * ab0
kg1     = (kq1 > 20 && kq1 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb1     portk kg1, 0.004, ib[1]
ab1     interp kb1, 0, 0, ib[1]
asum    += a1 * iw[1] * ab1
kg2     = (kq2 > 20 && kq2 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb2     portk kg2, 0.004, ib[2]
ab2     interp kb2, 0, 0, ib[2]
asum    += a2 * iw[2] * ab2
kg3     = (kq3 > 20 && kq3 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb3     portk kg3, 0.004, ib[3]
ab3     interp kb3, 0, 0, ib[3]
asum    += a3 * iw[3] * ab3
kg4     = (kq4 > 20 && kq4 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb4     portk kg4, 0.004, ib[4]
ab4     interp kb4, 0, 0, ib[4]
asum    += a4 * iw[4] * ab4
kg5     = (kq5 > 20 && kq5 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb5     portk kg5, 0.004, ib[5]
ab5     interp kb5, 0, 0, ib[5]
asum    += a5 * iw[5] * ab5
kg6     = (kq6 > 20 && kq6 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb6     portk kg6, 0.004, ib[6]
ab6     interp kb6, 0, 0, ib[6]
asum    += a6 * iw[6] * ab6
kg7     = (kq7 > 20 && kq7 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb7     portk kg7, 0.004, ib[7]
ab7     interp kb7, 0, 0, ib[7]
asum    += a7 * iw[7] * ab7
kg8     = (kq8 > 20 && kq8 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb8     portk kg8, 0.004, ib[8]
ab8     interp kb8, 0, 0, ib[8]
asum    += a8 * iw[8] * ab8
kg9     = (kq9 > 20 && kq9 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kb9     portk kg9, 0.004, ib[9]
ab9     interp kb9, 0, 0, ib[9]
asum    += a9 * iw[9] * ab9
; The glide factor: biquad output scales with frequency^-3/2, so a mode that moves with the
; key or the slack keeps its level. iden is set HERE, inside the reinit section: an
; i-only expression in a k-line after rireturn is folded once, on the build pass.
iden    = ikc * igl
kvl     = (kcs * kg) / iden
asig    = asum * inrm * kvl * sqrt(kvl) * kvol1
        rireturn

kettle.note: what loads the head. 0: a free ideal membrane, inharmonic Bessel spacings, a thump with no clear note. 1: the kettle-loaded timpano head, partials near 1:1.5:2, a singing note. The key stays on (1,1).

membrane.gloss: a free head: a thump with inharmonic overtones, no clear note

between.gloss: a note starts to come out of the thump

timpani.gloss: a kettledrum: a singing, tuned note

strike.note: where on the radius the stick lands. 0.65 is the timpanist's spot, full and round; 0.85 near the rim wakes more high modes and thins the note. The centre is left out: the note's mode has a node there.

playing spot.gloss: the timpanist's spot: full and round

quarter.gloss: a quarter of the radius in from the rim, a little brighter

rim.gloss: near the rim: thinner, more overtones

slack.note: how far a hard stroke stretches the head: the note starts sharp and falls back onto the key as the ring dies. 0.21 at full velocity is +165 cents at the stroke, at a 220 Hz key +50 after 0.1 s; soft strokes bend less.

tight.gloss: the pitch stands from the first instant

loose.gloss: a hard hit starts a touch sharp and settles

slack.gloss: a loose head: a big hit drops onto its note

mallet.note: how hard the stick is: its contact corner as a multiple of the played pitch. 1 is a soft felt, dark, mostly the note; 8 a hard stick, bright, every upper mode awake. The attack peak moves about 1.4 dB.

felt.gloss: a soft felt beater: dark and round

wood.gloss: a hard stick: bright, with a click

heard.hinweis: Neuer Körper, bisher nur gemessen (Gate, Tonhöhe, Anschlagspitze, zweite Note, CPU bei 44,1 und 176,4 kHz), von niemandem gehört. timpani/pauke und taiko benennen reale Instrumente und sind gegen eine Aufnahme zu beurteilen.

techniques.why: The TR-808 bass drum after Werner, Abel & Smith (DAFx-14): a barely damped bridged-T resonator struck by the trigger pulse, its ring thrown up while the 6 ms pulse is on, then the 'sigh', about two semitones settling over 0.2 s. One mode, no separate click, tone or drive; not a 909 or an acoustic kick. It follows the key, so a long decay on a low note is also the long 808 bass. The 6 ms throw is fixed in time, not in periods: at 55 Hz a soft knock, at 880 Hz an audible chirp. After 0.2 s it is a pure decaying sine at the key. It rings only while the synth's voice lives, so a long decay needs a long release. A new strike restarts the resonator: every hit has the same level, and a hit into a ring cuts that ring. The scale 1.6 is a level choice, not part of the model.
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; The TR-808 bass drum as Werner, Abel & Smith model its circuit (DAFx-14, "A Physically-
; Informed, Circuit-Bendable, Digital Model of the Roland TR-808 Bass Drum Circuit"): a
; bridged-T resonator, barely damped, struck by the trigger pulse. While the pulse is on
; it loads the network and throws the ring's frequency up by more than an octave for about
; 6 ms; afterwards a slow leak (R161) lets the ring settle about two semitones down over
; some 0.2 s, the "sigh". The output stage is linear: no drive, no separate click or tone.
kdecay  = 0.30   ; decay[0.08..1.0]: seconds for the ring to fall to 1/e, about -8.7 dB
ksweep  = 1.20   ; sweep[0..2]: octaves the ring is thrown up while the 6 ms trigger pulse is on
kbase   = kfreq * koct1
; THE RESONATOR IS `mvmfilter`, NOT `mode`: it rotates its state, so a frequency change
; under a ring moves the pitch and not the energy (`mode` gains up to +18 dB when its
; frequency falls while it rings). Frequency and tau are BOTH k-rate -- an a-rate
; frequency with a k-rate tau does not ring at all. It sits INSIDE the reinit section,
; so every strike restarts it from rest: each hit has the same level, and a hit into a
; ring cuts that ring (a one-sample step, as large as the ring was at that moment).
; THE STRIKE is the host's note-on edge. `mpulse` in the section also fires once when the
; orchestra is built; `kup` is 0 then, and that pulse has no amplitude.
kup     timeinsts
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit KICK
        endif
KICK:
iamp    = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1.0 : 0)
acon    mpulse iamp, 0
; the throw: full for 5 ms, back over 1 ms -- FIXED IN TIME, not in periods of the note
katk    linseg 1, 0.005, 1, 0.001, 0, 1, 0
; the sigh: 1.13 -> 1.0 over 0.18 s, read off the paper's Fig. 11 by eye
ksig    expseg 1.13, 0.18, 1, 1, 1
kf      limit kbase * 2^(ksweep * katk) * ksig, 20, 12000
ares    mvmfilter acon, kf, kdecay
        rireturn
; LEVEL CHOICE, not a correction of the model. An impulse of 1 into mvmfilter peaks at
; exactly 1 at every frequency, decay and rate; the host leaves a trig-struck body
; untrimmed, so this constant IS its loudness in the plugin (about 0.5 delivered, where
; the trimmed standing bodies peak).
asig    = ares * 1.6 * kvol1

decay.note: Seconds for the ring to fall to 1/e: 0.08 is down 60 dB in about 0.55 s, 1.0 in about 7 s. Read all the time, so turning it also shortens or lengthens a ring already sounding.

short.gloss: a short thud, down 60 dB in about half a second

default.gloss: a boom that falls 60 dB in about 2 s

long.gloss: the long boom that is also a bass note, about 7 s to -60 dB

sweep.note: Octaves the ring is thrown up while the 6 ms trigger pulse is on. It leaves the sigh and the ring after it as they are, and acts only in those 6 ms, so a change is heard from the next strike.

none.gloss: no throw: the strike starts on the sigh, a round soft onset

default.gloss: about 1.2 octaves up for 6 ms, a knock on the front

hard.gloss: two octaves up for 6 ms, a hard knock; a chirp on high keys

heard.hinweis: Ungehört. Der Vergleich mit einer Aufnahme einer echten TR-808-Bassdrum steht aus; der Eintrag trägt den Namen dieses Instruments.

techniques.why: The TR-808 snare as its Service Notes draw it: two bridged-T shell resonators struck by the trigger pulse, the lower on the key and the upper an octave above, and white noise through a 1.8 kHz high-pass under its own 0.2 s envelope, the snares. Shell Qs 17.4/10.7 after K. J. Werner, from a secondary source. The shell follows the key, the snares' colour does not: at 55 Hz a low, tom-like boom under the hiss, at 1760 Hz a 3 ms tick the snares carry. No rimshot, no accent; not an acoustic snare, and for metal use metal_squares. Every strike draws new noise, so at full snappy hits differ by up to 2.4 dB (about 1.4 dB over 30 strikes). It rings only while the synth's voice lives, so a long decay needs a long release. A new strike restarts shell and snares and cuts what still rings. The levels 0.4/0.25 and 3.08 are choices, not part of the model.
techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: snappy
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes
; The TR-808 snare drum as its Service Notes draw it (p. 6): two bridged-T resonators, the
; shell, struck by the trigger pulse, and white noise through a high-pass under its own
; envelope, the snares. VR8 (TONE) balances the two shell modes, VR9 (SNAPPY) sets the
; noise. Shell frequencies (rev. A 249.6 / 499.0 Hz) and Qs (17.4 / 10.7) are K. J.
; Werner's, quoted in "808 Snare Mutations" (norgatronics.blogspot.com, 2021), a SECONDARY
; source. Here the lower mode sits on the key and the upper an octave above (499.0 / 249.6).
ktone   = 0.50   ; tone[0..1]: level of the upper shell mode against the lower (VR8)
ksnappy = 0.50   ; snappy[0..1]: amplitude of the noise envelope against the shell (VR9)
kdecay  = 1.00   ; decay[1.0..3.0]: both shell Qs scaled together, 1 = the circuit's own
kbase   = kfreq * koct1
; THE NOISE runs free, outside the reinit, so every strike draws a new stretch of it. The
; seed is a HASH of the voice: Csound's 31-bit `rand` is the multiplicative Park-Miller
; generator, so seeds that are multiples of one another give voices that copy each other.
; frac(ivoice * 0.618...) does that (voices 1 and 2 at +0.50 correlation); this one keeps
; all 120 pairs of the 16 voices under 0.02.
an      rand 0.5, frac(abs(sin(ivoice * 12.9898)) * 43758.5453), 1
; THE STRIKE is the host's note-on edge. `mpulse` in the section also fires once when the
; orchestra is built; `kup` is 0 then, and that pulse has no amplitude.
kup     timeinsts
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit SNARESTRIKE
        endif
SNARESTRIKE:
iamp    = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1.0 : 0)
acon    mpulse iamp, 0
; the snares' envelope, restarted by every strike: up in 0.5 ms, down to a tenth in 60 ms,
; out over 0.2 s. The 0.001 that expsega needs is taken off again below, so the noise is
; exactly silent between strikes.
anv     expsega 0.001, 0.0005, iamp+0.001, 0.06, 0.1*iamp+0.001, 0.2, 0.001, 1, 0.001
; THE SHELL is two `mvmfilter`s, not `mode`: they rotate their state, so a key change under
; a ring (legato) moves the pitch and not the energy. Frequency and tau are both k-rate; tau =
; Q / (pi f) is each mode's 1/e time. INSIDE the reinit: every strike starts the shell from
; rest, as the other struck bodies do (left outside, a roll piled the rings up to asig 12).
; A mode above 16 kHz is switched off rather than parked below it.
kf1     limit kbase, 20, 16000
kf2     limit kbase * 2, 20, 16000
kg1     = (kbase < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg2     = (kbase * 2 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
a1      mvmfilter acon, kf1, 17.4 * kdecay / (3.14159 * kf1)
a2      mvmfilter acon, kf2, 10.7 * kdecay / (3.14159 * kf2)
        rireturn
aenv    = anv - 0.001
; tone moves level between the modes with their sum held at 1.3, so the strike's first
; sample, where both rings start together, does not change with tone (below an 8 kHz key;
; above it the upper mode is off and tone only takes level away).
ash     = a1 * kg1 * (1 - 0.7 * ktone) + a2 * kg2 * (0.3 + 0.7 * ktone)
; THE SNARES' colour does not follow the key. The circuit has no low-pass: the two 16 kHz
; ones and sqrt(sr/44100) hold the noise to one band at 44100 and 176400 (rms within 0.4 dB;
; its sample peak still reads about 1 dB higher at the plugin rate).
anh     buthp an * aenv, 1800   ; body resonance, FIXED in Hz
anl     butlp anh, 16000        ; body resonance, FIXED in Hz
anl     butlp anl, 16000        ; body resonance, FIXED in Hz
; LEVEL CHOICE, not part of the model: shell 0.4 against snares 0.25, and 3.08 puts one
; strike at the defaults on an asig peak of 1.60, on its first sample. The host leaves a
; struck body untrimmed, so this constant is its loudness in the plugin.
asig    = (ash * 0.4 + anl * sqrt(sr / 44100) * ksnappy * 0.25) * 3.08 * kvol1

tone.note: Level of the upper shell mode, an octave above the key, against the lower one on the key (VR8); their sum is held (keys under 8 kHz). The upper mode dies about three times faster, so 1 is brighter and shorter.

low.gloss: the lower mode leads: a round, darker shell on the key

high.gloss: the octave leads: a brighter, shorter knock

snappy.note: Amplitude of the snares' noise against the shell (VR9). It adds hiss and some level. The noise is new with every strike, so at 1 no two hits are quite the same; 0 leaves the bare shell.

none.gloss: no snares: the bare two-mode shell, a tuned knock

full.gloss: the snares lead: a crack of hiss over the shell

decay.note: Both shell Qs scaled together; 1 is the circuit's own. At 220 Hz the shell falls 60 dB in 0.16 s at 1 and 0.47 s at 3; the snares keep their 0.2 s. Read all the time, so it also reshapes a ring already sounding.

tight.gloss: the circuit's own ring: a short tuned knock under the snares

ringing.gloss: twice the ring, the shell's pitch clearly heard

long.gloss: three times the ring: a tuned drum that sings past the snares

heard.hinweis: Ungehört. Der Vergleich mit einer Aufnahme einer echten TR-808-Snare steht aus; der Eintrag trägt den Namen dieses Instruments. Gate: die Eckenregel verfehlt bei vollem snappy knapp (1,07 dB bei 44100, 1,15 dB bei 176400 gegen 1,00), weil die Spitze dort Kessel plus Rauschen ist und vom Rauschzug abhängt (über 2720 Züge Median 0,55 dB, rund 10 % über 1 dB); alles andere besteht, auch `moves` ohne Textur-Ausnahme.

techniques.why: gong / tam-tam / anvil / metallic percussion (a singing bowl is `singing_bowl`, a different body with a definite pitch): two phase-modulation operators standing on the (3,0) and (4,0) modes Chladni's law predicts for a free circular plate, driving one carrier and a second carrier a few Hz above it. The exponent of that law is the instrument's main axis, so the metal runs from a tight nearly-pitched body to a wide plate with no note left; each mode has its own decay, so the attack is bright and the tail is not. Since the migration to three operators this entry has the topology Hayes & Saitis 2020 measured -- two modulators in linear combination on ONE carrier's phase -- so under BJ's scope ruling of 2026-07-29 (that source concerns FM entries only) their word-to-parameter directions now apply here as they do to `fm3`: `index` is their modulator gain, `stretch` sets both their tuning ratios. Before the migration it was `foscili` with the ratio hardcoded at 2.41 and no knob on it at all, which is what docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §4.8 records as "what the designers reached for hardest has no knob here".

stretch.note: how far the metal's modes stand off a harmonic series. This is not a free number: it is the exponent p of Chladni's law, f = C(m+2n)^p, and the two operators are placed at the (3,0) and (4,0) modes it predicts. The range is the published one for cymbals, handbells and church bells. Low is a tight metal that still carries the note; high is a wide plate whose partials no longer add up to a pitch. It is ALSO the two modulator tuning ratios at once, because the law computes them from p. WORD DIRECTION, MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED -- Hayes & Saitis 2020, thirty sound designers steering this exact topology (Fig. 4, Spearman): the modulator TUNING RATIO is the single largest correlate of `bright` (0.56/0.54, p<.001) and joint-largest of `rough` (0.42/0.56), both POSITIVE -- for either word, raise this. `thick` goes the other way (-0.28, p<.01). Their scope ruling and the full reading: docs/LCO_TIMBRE_SEMANTICS.md §2 and §4.8.

tight.gloss: the modes closest together: a small, nearly-pitched metal

bell.gloss: the middle of the published range: struck bell, the note still there

plate.gloss: a flat circular plate, the value the law gives for one: gong

wide.gloss: the top of the published range: the partials furthest apart, no note left

index.note: how hard the two modes are driven -- how many partials the metal carries. Low leaves the note almost bare; high fills the spectrum between the modes and loosens the pitch, because a deep index empties the carrier itself. WORD DIRECTION, MEASURED -- Hayes & Saitis 2020 (Fig. 4, Spearman): the modulator GAIN is what designers raised for `bright` (0.41/0.52, p<.001) and harder still for `rough` (0.63/0.51). Both positive. DECLARED, from the same paper: on FM `bright` and `rough` are very nearly the SAME move, and the authors say why -- "it is challenging to increase the energy in high frequency components without also increasing inharmonicity". This entry can carry `bright` faithfully; it will not separate `rough` from it by these means. Roughness has to come from partials close enough to interact -- a modal bank or a detuned stack -- not from sidebands.

struck softly.gloss: barely driven: the note with a trace of metal on it

struck.gloss: an ordinary strike, the modes clearly there

struck hard.gloss: hard: the spectrum fills in between the modes

hammered.gloss: hammered, the pitch beginning to loosen

crashed.gloss: everything the two modes can put out

damping.note: how much faster a mode dies for standing higher. Kirchhoff's plate equation has two loss terms: one that damps every mode alike -- that is `ring` -- and one that grows with the mode's frequency. This is the second one. At zero the metal is damped evenly and keeps its colour for as long as the note lasts; turned up, the modes the law puts furthest out go first, and what is left is the plain low body. A held note keeps driving the plate, so a mode that dies faster also stands lower the whole way through -- this is not only an attack shape.

even.gloss: no frequency-dependent loss at all: every mode falls at the same rate and the metal holds its colour to the end of the note

metal.gloss: the default: the (4,0) mode dies about twice as fast as the body and stands about half as high -- an ordinary struck metal

dead top.gloss: the top is gone in a fifth of the time and sits 20 dB down: the low body alone, still ringing

ring.note: how long the drive holds before the metal darkens. Low collapses to a plain body almost at once; high stays lit deep into the note. The host owns when the note stops -- this is the colour, not the loudness.

quick.gloss: the metal darkens almost at once

long.gloss: stays lit well into the note

beat.note: how fast the two struck bodies swell against each other. NOT a detune: the offset is a fraction of a Hertz and you never hear it as pitch, you hear the two bodies going in and out of step -- BJ, 2026-07-31, on the name it used to carry: „das ist kein detune“. The swell has to be SLOW: the n-th partial swells n times as fast as the first, so an offset near 1 Hz makes the third partial pulse almost four times a second, which he heard as hectic. The whole axis stays under 0.5 Hz. At zero the two lock and the body stands still -- the static escape, and about 2.7 dB louder, because two bodies in step add where two bodies beating do not.

locked.gloss: the two bodies in step: one still body, and the loudest setting

slow.gloss: 0.2 Hz: one swell every five seconds

wide.gloss: 0.43 Hz: the fastest swell this body offers

techniques.code:
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kidx    = 0.53   ; index[0.0..1.0]: how hard the two modes are driven -- how many partials the
                 ;   metal carries, and how far the pitch of the note loosens
kstr    = 1.70   ; stretch[1.40..2.40]: Chladni's exponent p in f = C(m+2n)^p. The published
                 ;   range for cymbals, handbells and church bells; about 2 is a flat circular
                 ;   plate, the gong end. Low is a tight, nearly-pitched metal
kring   = 0.56   ; ring[0.0..1.0]: how long the drive holds before the metal darkens
kdmp    = 0.35   ; damping[0.0..1.0]: how much faster the upper mode dies than the lower one
; LOUDNESS: beat
kbeat   = 0.50   ; beat[0.0..1.0]: how fast the two struck bodies swell against each other
; --- the two ratios are COMPUTED from the law, not chosen. Modes (2,0) (3,0) (4,0) of a
;     free circular plate have (m+2n) = 2, 3, 4, so f_k / f_2 = (k/2)^p
kr2     = pow(1.5, kstr)         ; operator 2 stands ON the (3,0) mode
kr3     = pow(2.0, kstr)         ; operator 3 stands ON the (4,0) mode
; --- Kirchhoff's plate equation carries TWO loss terms (Schaefer, Werner & Rabenstein,
;     "Physical Modeling of Vibrating Plates", DAGA 2019 Rostock, 299-302, eq. 1). d1 is
;     frequency-independent and "leads to a uniform damping for all oscillation modes" --
;     that is `ring`. d3 scales with the squared wavenumber, and since the squared
;     wavenumber goes with the mode's FREQUENCY (eq. 15), the decay rate of eq. 14 is
;     affine in the mode ratio: the higher a mode stands, the faster it dies. d3 is
;     `damping`. A held note keeps driving the plate, and a driven damped mode settles at
;     drive/rate -- so a mode that dies q times faster also STANDS q times lower. That is
;     the steady state of the same equation, not a number fitted to a result.
ktau    = 0.15 + 6.0 * kring * kring
kd3     = 3.0 * kdmp * kdmp
kq2     = 1 + kd3 * (kr2 - 1)               ; mode (3,0) decays this many times faster
kq3     = 1 + kd3 * (kr3 - 1)               ; mode (4,0), standing higher, faster still
kf2     = 0.30 / kq2                        ; and sits that much lower while driven
kf3     = 0.30 / kq3
kenv2   = kf2 + (1 - kf2) * exp(-knote * kq2 / ktau)
kenv3   = kf3 + (1 - kf3) * exp(-knote * kq3 / ktau)
ksw     oscili 0.30, 0.31, giSine   ; slow, free-running: which mode carries the metal
ki2     = kidx * 0.60 * kenv2 * (1 - ksw)
ki3     = kidx * 0.42 * kenv3 * (1 + ksw)
; --- Nyquist, Carson's rule per operator and summed -- both modulators arrive on ONE carrier
;     phase, so the deviation that counts is their SUM and the room is shared. `fm3` records
;     what happens otherwise: "bounding each operator as if it were alone is what put a
;     49 kHz sideband on a 440 Hz note". What is reserved is what an operator
;     can EVER ask for -- `index` at the top of its range, envelope at 1, ksw at its peak --
;     never what it is asking for right now. A guard that divides by the live index divides
;     the envelope and the axis straight back out: every common factor of ki2 and ki3
;     cancels against kneed, and where the guard bites, `ring`, `damping` and `index` stop
;     doing anything at all. Measured 2026-07-31 before this line was written: at 1760 Hz,
;     stretch 2.4, damping 0, three `ring` settings rendered BIT-IDENTICAL and moves() went
;     False. `fm3` already reserves from an operator's peak for this reason. kroom has a
;     FLOOR and not a zero, because a body whose room reaches zero is a bare sine with every
;     axis dead. DECLARED LIMIT, measured 2026-07-31 and shared with `fm3`: the 20000 ceiling
;     dates from when the page and the plugin still ran at 1x, and against it this pot is
;     already at its floor by A7 -- at 3520 Hz the body is close to a sine and its colour
;     travels 9 Hz, under the movement gate. Every register up to and including A6 moves.
kpk2    = 0.60 * 1.30
kpk3    = 0.42 * 1.30
kroom   limit (min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc) - 1 - kr2 - kr3, 0.5, 4000
kneed   = 6.2832 * (kpk2 * kr2 + kpk3 * kr3)
kscl    = min(1, kroom / max(kneed, 0.001))  ; one factor for both, so their balance holds
ki2s    = ki2 * kscl
ki3s    = ki3 * kscl
; --- two modulators on one carrier's phase, and a second carrier a few Hz above, so the
;     pair beats the way two struck metal bodies do
am2     poscil ki2s, kc * kr2, giSine
am3     poscil ki3s, kc * kr3, giSine
kbea    = 0.5 * kbeat           ; Hz, so the SLOWEST partial beats at kbea and the
                                ;   n-th at n*kbea -- which is why this has to stay well
                                ;   under 1 Hz: at 1.3 Hz the third partial beat 3.9 times
                                ;   a second and BJ heard it as hectic (2026-07-31)
acr1    tablei (phasor:a(kc)) + am2 + am3, giSine, 1, 0, 1
acr2    tablei (phasor:a(kc + kbea)) + am2 + am3, giSine, 1, 0, 1
asum    = acr1 * 0.60 + acr2 * 0.40
aref    poscil 0.45, kc                     ; steady level reference
; The level stage sees ONE voice, not the pair. A follower fast enough for the spectral
; onset (10 Hz) is by definition fast enough to FLATTEN a beat slower than that, and at
; ihp=1 it still swallows anything under a Hz -- docs/LCO_CONCEPT.md l.173 records that
; `fm_bell`'s ihp=1 "exists to protect its doublet beat", and this body's beat is slower
; than either follower. Taking the gain from the first voice alone holds the loudness and
; leaves the beat in. Measured: 2.4 dB of swell before, 14.8 dB after, at the rate asked for
krms1   rms acr1, 10
krmsr   rms aref, 10
kg      = krmsr / (krms1 + 0.0001)
asig    = asum * kg
asig    = asig * kvol1

heard.hinweis: BJ hat diesen Eintrag über eine Stunde auf der Parameterseite gehört und dabei ZWEIMAL positiv geurteilt — „überzeugend“ und „alles gut bis auf …“. Was offen ist, ist NICHT der Eintrag, sondern das Gegenhören der drei Korrekturen, die seine Befunde ausgelöst haben: (1) das Schweben lief bei 1,3 Hz, der dritte Teilton also 3,9-mal pro Sekunde — jetzt 0,5·beat, höchstens zweimal in vier Sekunden; (2) `detune` war unhörbar, weil `balance` mit 10 Hz jedes langsamere Schweben glattzog — der Pegel kommt jetzt aus EINER Stimme, 2,4 dB Hub vorher, 14,8 dB nachher, und die Achse heißt `beat`; (3) `damping` erreichte nur Operator 3 und nur dessen Zeitkonstante — jetzt der d3-Term der Plattengleichung, Schwerpunkt bei 3 s 712 / 445 / 317 Hz über die drei Anker. Ein leerer Status hier hätte diese Stunde gelöscht.

techniques.why:
singing bowl / Klangschale / Tibetan bowl: a bank of `mode` resonators on the (j,0) modes of an axisymmetric shell, every mode a PAIR split by a measured fraction, struck by a mallet or rubbed into a mode lock-in. It exists because `metallic_fm` -- a Chladni free circular plate, and a good gong -- is the wrong body for the word, and the mismatch is objective rather than a matter of taste: that entry computes its two ratios from Chladni's law as 1.5^p and 2.0^p over a declared p of [1.4, 2.4], and a bowl's first two overtones at 2.83 and 5.42 would need p = 2.57 for the one operator and 2.44 for the other -- two different exponents, both outside the range. Rendered at its defaults at 220 Hz its loudest low partial sits at 62 Hz: it does not carry the note. BJ, 2026-07-29: „Crystal singing bowls in a cathedral“ comes out extremely dissonant, „Wäre gut da eine eigene Parametrisierung zu machen (oder Instrument)“.

THE POINT OF THE BODY, in the source's own sentence: ‚The frequency relationships are mildly inharmonic, which does not affect the definite pitch of this instrument, mainly dominated by the first (2,0) shell mode.‘ A bowl has a DEFINITE PITCH. That is exactly what a gong does not have and exactly what was missing.

SOURCES, both read in full, both quoted in docs/plans/PLAN_lco_singing_bowl.md with their tables: Inácio, Henrique & Antunes, ‚The dynamics of Tibetan singing bowls‘, Acta Acustica united with Acustica 92 (2006) 637-653 -- experimental modal identification of four bowls, which supplies the mode series, the pair splits and the damping range; and Terwagne & Bush, ‚Tibetan singing bowls‘, arXiv:1106.6348 -- the closed form f(j,0) ~ j(j^2-1)/sqrt(j^2+1), the finding that only (n,0) modes are excited at all, and the rubbed mode lock-in that `sung` runs on. Nothing here is fitted: the two ends of the main axis are two bowls somebody measured.

DECLARED PROPERTIES, because an author has to be able to route this without hearing it first. It FOLLOWS `kfreq` -- the whole bank stands on kc, and the (2,0) mode is the note. It DECAYS (`; DECAY: SELF`): struck, it rings down on its own, and at the long end of `ring` that ring-down is far longer than any note this instrument plays -- Q 5228 at the default is a 1/e time of 7.6 s -- so inside a 0.1-11 s note it is a standing tone that darkens. Rubbed (`sung` 1.0) it stands outright, which is what a rubbed bowl does.

WHAT IT MEASURES AND IS NOT: it is FLAT ACROSS THE KEYBOARD, which was not true before the exciter was repaired and is worth stating because of that. At the attack: 110 +4.73, 220 +2.99, 440 +0.40, 880 +4.50 dB -- 4.34 dB of spread and -0.08 dB per octave, i.e. scatter and not a slope. `mode`'s gain at resonance does go with Q over frequency, and the library's other mode banks show it (`driven_metal` -2.72, `drum_head` -2.99 dB/octave); here the strike is broadband enough that it does not read as a tilt. What DOES stay over the one-loudness bound is the corner space: 8.01 dB across the 81 corners at 220 Hz and 12.67 dB across corners and registers together, and most of that is `sung`, whose two halves are one strike and no strike. Declared, not flattened. Post-onset peak at the rate the plugin runs Csound (176400 -- `lroOsFactor_` is 4 in PluginProcessor.h, capped at 200 kHz), with the instance old enough that none of the build-time strike is left: 0.76 at 220 Hz at the defaults, and 2.20 at the loudest corner the body has -- 110 Hz, `ring` free, `warble` at its narrowest -- against a clip ceiling of 2.52 transparent and 2.75 absolute. So it clips nowhere, and it is quieter at its defaults than the library's other mode banks are at theirs (`struck_bar` 1.96, `cymbal` 2.26). That is the price of a corner space this wide and it is declared rather than hidden.

bowl.note: which measured bowl the mode series is. Not a curve and not a stretch factor: the two ends are Inácio et al. Table I/II, Bowl 2 (563 g, 152 mm, the flattest of their four) and Bowl 4 (the widest), so every position between them is between two real instruments. Bowl 2 runs 1, 2.7, 4.8, 7.5, 10.6, 14.2; Bowl 4 runs 1, 2.9, 5.7, 9.1, 13.1, 17.7, which sits almost exactly on the in-plane ring solution f_j ~ j(j^2-1)/sqrt(j^2+1) that Terwagne & Bush validate for j = 2..6. What it moves is where the partials SIT, not how bright the body is: from 0.0 to 1.0 at 220 Hz the (3,0) pair travels 593.5 to 637.5 Hz -- 124 cents -- and the (4,0) 1054 to 1259 Hz, while the spectral centroid stays within 1 Hz. So it retunes the inharmonicity and leaves the colour alone. It is not a level control either: 0.30 dB across its own travel.

small.gloss: Bowl 2 as measured: the flattest series, the partials closest in

wide.gloss: Bowl 4 as measured, and the ring solution: the partials furthest out

warble.note: how far the two halves of each mode pair stand apart -- the bowl's beating, and a measurement rather than a detune. Every mode in Inácio et al. Table I is a PAIR (f_nA, f_nB) because a real bowl is not perfectly axisymmetric; their model ‚introduc[es] a difference (or split) between the frequencies of each mode pair‘, and Terwagne & Bush confirm it independently: ‚Due to the bowl asymmetry, two peaks separated by several Hz arise and a beating mode is heard.‘ The pattern up the bank is IRREGULAR and that is the point -- Bowl 1's seven pairs measure 0.454, 0.131, 0.334, 0.017, 0.375, 0.038, 0.299 %, which have no common period, so twelve long-ringing partials never come back into phase together. One shared fraction was the first version and it was audible as a pulse. This axis scales the whole measured pattern; the shape is the bowl's. At 0.0 the split is 0.3x Bowl 1 (a 3.3 s beat at 220 Hz), at 0.164 Bowl 1 exactly, at 1.0 Bowl 3's measured 2.07 %. DECLARED AS THE LOUDNESS AXIS (`; LOUDNESS: warble`): because the body is read at the note's peak and the peak of a beat depends on where the halves are in their cycle, it moves the peak 3.56 dB on its own at 220 Hz. That is the beating, not a fader. For comparison, on the same measurement `bowl` moves 0.30 dB and `ring` 1.16 -- the strike really is the same at every Q, which is what its own note claims.

slow.gloss: the pair barely apart: one beat every three seconds at 220 Hz

measured.gloss: Bowl 1 exactly as the table has it: about one beat per second at 220 Hz

wide.gloss: Bowl 3's 2.07 %, the widest pair the paper measured: a fast shimmer

ring.note: how long the shell holds, and the range is the paper's: ‚dissipation is very low, with modal damping ratios typically in the range 0.002~0.015 % (higher values pertaining to higher-order modes). However, note that these values may increase one order of magnitude, or more, depending on how the bowls are actually supported or handled.‘ Q = 1/(2*zeta), so 25000 for a bowl standing free down to a few hundred for one held in a hand. The upper modes are damped harder than the fundamental (factors 1.3 to 3.5 up the bank), which is the paper's own direction and is why the note darkens as it rings. THE STRIKE DOES NOT CHANGE WITH IT, and that is measured rather than assumed: over a 75x span of Q a fixed impulse into one `mode` gives an attack of -69.5 to -68.3 dB while the DECAY goes from -102.0 dB over 5.7 s to -1.4. An earlier version divided the exciter by Q on the theory that a resonator's gain goes with Q -- true of its steady state, not of its response to a strike -- and that made this a 15 dB volume control. It does NOT change the level: 2.80 at 110 Hz and 2.24 at 220 against a clip ceiling of 2.75, both at `ring` 1.0, because the strike is the same at every Q.

held.gloss: the bowl in a hand, the paper's damped case: Q ~500, gone in about five seconds

mid.gloss: Q ~5200: a 7.6 s 1/e time, so it stands and darkens through any note

free.gloss: the lowest damping measured, Q 25000: it outlasts the longest note by far

sung.note: struck or rubbed, and they are two different spectra from one body. Terwagne & Bush: ‚When the bowl is rubbed with a leather wrapped mallet, the lowest mode is excited along with its harmonics, an effect known as a mode lock in.‘ So struck (0.0) gives the inharmonic shell modes above, and rubbed (1.0) gives the (2,0) mode plus TRUE HARMONICS of it -- which is why the lock-in is its own layer and not a retuning of the bank. The pair beats on that layer too, because the rub excites both halves of the fundamental. It crossfades equal-power over 0.35 s, because friction takes hold rather than jumping; added instead of crossfaded it measured 22.3 dB across its own travel. The two halves are levelled THROUGH the note, not at its peak: over four seconds at 220 Hz they measure -15.10 and -15.77 dB rms, 0.7 dB apart. What remains at the PEAK is 6.7 dB, and it is structural -- the struck body decays from its strike and the rubbed one has no strike at all, so the two cannot match at the peak AND through the note. This levelling favours where the note actually lives.

struck.gloss: the mallet: shell modes, mildly inharmonic, ringing down

half.gloss: the rub taking hold over the strike

rubbed.gloss: the mode lock-in: fundamental plus true harmonics, standing

techniques.code:
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: warble
; A Tibetan singing bowl as what the measurements say it is: an axisymmetric shell whose
; (j,0) modes are MILDLY inharmonic and therefore keep a definite pitch -- Inacio, Henrique
; & Antunes, Acta Acustica 92 (2006) 637-653, on four bowls they identified experimentally.
; That is the whole difference to `metallic_fm`, which is a Chladni plate and has no pitch.
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kbowl   = 0.50   ; bowl[0.0..1.0]: which measured bowl the mode series is
kwarb   = 0.30   ; warble[0.0..1.0]: how far the two halves of each mode pair stand apart
kring   = 0.60   ; ring[0.0..1.0]: how long the shell holds
ksung   = 0.00   ; sung[0.0..1.0]: struck (shell modes) -> rubbed (mode lock-in, harmonics)
; --- THE MODE SERIES. Two MEASURED bowls, not a curve through them: Bowl 2 (563 g, 152 mm)
;     is the flattest of the four and Bowl 4 the widest, and Bowl 4 sits almost exactly on
;     the in-plane ring solution f_j ~ j(j^2-1)/sqrt(j^2+1) that Terwagne & Bush validate
;     for j = 2..6 (arXiv:1106.6348 Eq. 5). `bowl` travels between the two, so every
;     position is between two real instruments.
kr2     = 1.0
kr3     = 2.70 + 0.20 * kbowl      ; Bowl 2: 2.7   Bowl 4: 2.9
kr4     = 4.80 + 0.90 * kbowl      ;         4.8          5.7
kr5     = 7.50 + 1.60 * kbowl      ;         7.5          9.1
kr6     = 10.60 + 2.50 * kbowl     ;        10.6         13.1
kr7     = 14.20 + 3.50 * kbowl     ;        14.2         17.7
; --- DAMPING. zeta 0.002..0.015 % measured, "higher values pertaining to higher-order
;     modes", and "may increase one order of magnitude, or more, depending on how the bowls
;     are actually supported or handled". Q = 1/(2*zeta): 25000 free, ~330 held. `ring` runs
;     that span; the per-mode factor is the paper's own direction and not a fitted number.
kz      = 0.00002 * exp(log(50.0) * (1 - kring))   ; 0.002 % .. 0.1 %
kq2     = 1 / (2 * kz)
kq3     = kq2 / 1.30
kq4     = kq2 / 1.70
kq5     = kq2 / 2.20
kq6     = kq2 / 2.80
kq7     = kq2 / 3.50
; --- THE SPLIT, and it is IRREGULAR up the bank, which is what Table I actually shows.
;     Bowl 1's seven measured pairs, as (f_B - f_A)/f_AB: 0.454, 0.131, 0.334, 0.017,
;     0.375, 0.038, 0.299 %. A single fraction for all of them was the first version and
;     it was wrong twice over -- unfaithful to the table, and audible: twelve long-ringing
;     partials whose beats share one period all come back into phase together, and the
;     peak of the note then sat 11.6 dB above the strike at the long end of `ring`, which
;     this project's own axis probe reads as a fader. The measured pattern has no common
;     period, so they never re-align. `warble` scales the whole pattern; the shape is the
;     bowl's.
kwsc    = 0.30 + 4.26 * kwarb                      ; Bowl 1 at 0.3x .. Bowl 3's 2.07 % on the fundamental
kw2     = 0.00454 * kwsc
kw3     = 0.00131 * kwsc
kw4     = 0.00334 * kwsc
kw5     = 0.00017 * kwsc
kw6     = 0.00375 * kwsc
kw7     = 0.00038 * kwsc
; --- THE EXCITER. Struck is a short burst into a shell that then rings on its own; rubbed
;     is continuous, and Terwagne & Bush record what continuous friction does: the lowest
;     mode locks in and brings its own HARMONICS with it. So `sung` crossfades the drive
;     from a strike into a hold AND fades in a harmonic layer locked to the fundamental.
; --- THE MALLET, and its amplitude does NOT depend on Q. Measured on one `mode` over a
;     75x span of Q, a fixed impulse gives an attack level of -69.5 to -68.3 dB -- 1.2 dB
;     across the whole range -- while what changes is the DECAY: -102.0 dB over 5.7 s at
;     Q 330 against -1.4 at Q 25000. That is what Q means and it is what the mallet does,
;     so `ring` is a decay axis with a constant strike and needs no normalisation. An
;     earlier version divided the impulse by Q on the theory that a resonator's gain goes
;     with Q; that is true of its STEADY state, not of its response to a strike, and it
;     made the axis a 15 dB volume control.
;     NO NOISE EXCITER, deliberately, and this one is also measured rather than reasoned:
;     at Q 10000 a mode's bandwidth is 0.02 Hz, so noise through it is one sinusoid whose
;     amplitude random-walks over tens of seconds -- the same body measured -24.3 dB at
;     three seconds and -33.3 at 5.7. `struck_bar` and `cymbal` can hold a noise exciter
;     because their Q is 900-1400; at a bowl's Q it is not a drive, it is a lottery.
;     THE MALLET IS COMPUTED AT A-RATE, AND BOTH OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVES ARE WRONG HERE.
;     `expon` starts when the INSTRUMENT starts, so under a preroll -- and under any host
;     that keeps a voice alive between notes -- the strike has already decayed before the
;     note begins: the axis probe read the peak 13.0 dB apart across `ring` where the
;     body's own sample peak moves 0.89 dB. Hanging it on `knote` instead cures that and
;     brings a worse fault, because 1.8 ms is SHORTER THAN ONE CONTROL PERIOD -- so how
;     much of the pulse exists depends on the control rate, and the control rate follows
;     the sample rate. Measured on the two rates that matter: 44100, where a body gets
;     auditioned, against 176400, which is what the plugin actually compiles Csound at
;     (`lroOsFactor_ { 4 }` in PluginProcessor.h, capped at 200 kHz). The same body peaked
;     2.049 and 12.48 -- a factor of 6.09 -- and its centroid fell 377 to 259 Hz. The bank
;     is not at fault: `mpulse` alone measures 1.07x across those rates, and `interp` in
;     place of `a()` changed nothing, so it is not the staircase either.
;     So the weight is the SAME one-pole force step, taken where a sub-millisecond force
;     belongs: at audio rate, as a `tone` on the contact, at the corner the exponential
;     already named. Across those two rates it now measures 1.04x with the centroid 362
;     against 361 Hz. It also costs two thirds of the register tilt (12.61 dB from 110 to
;     880 Hz, now 4.20) and brings the keyboard inside the host's clip ceiling -- 23.32 at
;     110 Hz before, 2.80 after -- because how much of a 1.8 ms pulse survived one control
;     period was a function of pitch as much as of rate.
;     AND IT IS DETERMINISTIC. A mallet is a short force pulse, not noise: an exponential
;     force step is broadband on its own (one-pole, corner 1/(2*pi*0.0018) = 88 Hz, so
;     every mode gets excited and the higher ones a little less, which is what a soft
;     mallet does). Multiplying it by `rand` made the note's PEAK a random draw, and the
;     axis probe then read `bowl` and `warble` as faders at 1.0 and 3.5 dB when neither
;     touches the level -- it was measuring noise peaks.
;     TWO PARTS, because one alone does not do it. The exponential force step is the
;     mallet's WEIGHT and rolls off at 88 Hz, so on its own it leaves the upper modes
;     nearly unexcited -- measured, the body's colour then travelled 1 Hz over the note
;     and `project_lco_movement_by_default` is a platform requirement, not a preference.
;     A single-sample `mpulse` is the CONTACT and is flat to Nyquist. Together they are a
;     soft mallet on a bowl: everything rings, the top rings less, and the top dies first,
;     which is the colour travelling 360 Hz over the note.
;     AND IT IS RE-STRUCK AT EVERY NOTE, which needs the `reinit` below and not a
;     comment. `mpulse kamp, 0` emits ONE impulse at the instance's first sample, and the
;     host scores a single always-on instance (`i 1 0 2000000000`), so without this the bowl
;     is struck once when the orchestra is BUILT and every note after it only un-gates
;     the decaying residue. Measured before this line, at 220 Hz with the defaults: a
;     note begun at 0 s of instance uptime peaked 1.6132, at 2 s 0.8837, at 8 s 0.3634,
;     at 30 s 0.0193 -- 38 dB of difference made by nothing but how long the plugin had
;     been open. `plucked_wire` carries the same construction and the same warning for
;     the same reason. `BOWLSTRIKE` is a LABEL: a second copy of this body in one
;     instrument needs a different one.
        if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
          reinit BOWLSTRIKE
        endif
BOWLSTRIKE:
acon    mpulse 3.0, 0                               ; the contact, flat to Nyquist
        rireturn
aw      tone acon, 88.4                             ; the weight, 1/(2*pi*0.0018) = 88.4 Hz
aex     = acon + aw                                 ; a soft mallet on a bowl
; --- the bank. Each mode twice, split by kw, so the pair beats the way the table says.
ka2a    limit kc * kr2 * (1 - kw2/2), 20, 18000
ka2b    limit kc * kr2 * (1 + kw2/2), 20, 18000
ka3a    limit kc * kr3 * (1 - kw3/2), 20, 18000
ka3b    limit kc * kr3 * (1 + kw3/2), 20, 18000
ka4a    limit kc * kr4 * (1 - kw4/2), 20, 18000
ka4b    limit kc * kr4 * (1 + kw4/2), 20, 18000
ka5a    limit kc * kr5 * (1 - kw5/2), 20, 18000
ka5b    limit kc * kr5 * (1 + kw5/2), 20, 18000
ka6a    limit kc * kr6 * (1 - kw6/2), 20, 18000
ka6b    limit kc * kr6 * (1 + kw6/2), 20, 18000
ka7a    limit kc * kr7 * (1 - kw7/2), 20, 18000
ka7b    limit kc * kr7 * (1 + kw7/2), 20, 18000
kg3     = (kc * kr3 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg4     = (kc * kr4 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg5     = (kc * kr5 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg6     = (kc * kr6 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
kg7     = (kc * kr7 < 16000 ? 1 : 0)
a2a     mode aex, ka2a, kq2
a2b     mode aex, ka2b, kq2
a3a     mode aex, ka3a, kq3
a3b     mode aex, ka3b, kq3
a4a     mode aex, ka4a, kq4
a4b     mode aex, ka4b, kq4
a5a     mode aex, ka5a, kq5
a5b     mode aex, ka5b, kq5
a6a     mode aex, ka6a, kq6
a6b     mode aex, ka6b, kq6
a7a     mode aex, ka7a, kq7
a7b     mode aex, ka7b, kq7
; --- the (2,0) mode dominates: "mainly dominated by the first (2,0) shell mode"
ashell  = (a2a + a2b) * 1.000 \
        + (a3a + a3b) * 0.500 * kg3 \
        + (a4a + a4b) * 0.280 * kg4 \
        + (a5a + a5b) * 0.160 * kg5 \
        + (a6a + a6b) * 0.090 * kg6 \
        + (a7a + a7b) * 0.050 * kg7
; --- MODE LOCK-IN, and it is a SEPARATE LAYER because it is a separate spectrum. Rubbed
;     rather than struck, "the lowest mode is excited along with its harmonics, an effect
;     known as a mode 'lock in'" (Terwagne & Bush). Those are true harmonics of the (2,0)
;     mode and not shell modes, so re-tuning the bank would be the wrong move. It is
;     deterministic and not noise-driven, which is what friction locking onto a mode IS,
;     and it also keeps this half of the axis off the random walk above.
;     The pair beats here too: the rub excites both halves of the fundamental.
alk     poscil 0.50, kc * (1 - kw2/2), giSine
alkb    poscil 0.50, kc * (1 + kw2/2), giSine
kh2     = (kc * 2 < 16000 ? 0.30 : 0)               ; the same Nyquist gate the shell
kh3     = (kc * 3 < 16000 ? 0.12 : 0)               ;   bank carries -- without it the
kh4     = (kc * 4 < 16000 ? 0.05 : 0)               ;   harmonics fold at 1x oversampling
alk2    poscil kh2, kc * 2, giSine
alk3    poscil kh3, kc * 3, giSine
alk4    poscil kh4, kc * 4, giSine
kbldr   portk ksung, 0.35                            ; the rub takes hold, it does not jump
kbld    limit kbldr, 0, 1                            ; sqrt of a negative NaNs the whole voice
; --- levelled against the strike THROUGH THE NOTE, not at its peak, and the difference
;     matters: the rub STANDS while the strike decays, so the two can be matched at one
;     or the other and not at both. Over a four-second note at 220 Hz they now measure
;     -15.10 and -15.77 dB rms, 0.7 dB apart. What is left at the PEAK is 6.7 dB, and
;     that is a strike against no strike -- it is what the axis MEANS, not a fader. An
;     earlier 0.227 was levelled against a strike that was itself wrong (see the reinit
;     above) and left this axis moving 14.06 dB. This is a level match between two layers
;     of this body, not a curve over anyone's model.
alock   = (alk + alkb + alk2 + alk3 + alk4) * 0.60
; --- ONE equal-power crossfade, so `sung` moves the spectrum and not the level. Added
;     rather than crossfaded, it measured 22.3 dB across its own travel.
asig    = ashell * 0.42 * sqrt(1 - kbld) + alock * sqrt(kbld)
; --- ONE output scale, and it is headroom rather than taste. The loudest thing this body
;     can be asked for is a LOW bowl left to ring with the pair barely split -- 110 Hz,
;     `ring` 1.0, `warble` 0.0 -- because `mode`'s gain at resonance goes with Q over
;     frequency and nothing beats the peak down. Measured there at the rate the plugin
;     runs Csound, and with the instance old enough that nothing of the build-time strike
;     is left: 0.50 puts that corner at 2.20, under the host's transparent ceiling of
;     2.52, and the defaults at 0.76 at 220 Hz. That is quieter than the library's other
;     mode banks at their own defaults (`struck_bar` 1.96, `cymbal` 2.26) and it is the
;     price of a body whose corner space is this wide: a scale that put the defaults
;     among them would clip the bass. It moves no balance inside the body.
asig    = asig * kvol1 * 0.50

techniques.why: TR-808 cymbal and hi-hat after Werner, Abel & Smith, ICMC-SMC 2014: six band-limited Schmitt-trigger squares at the circuit's 205.3/304.4/369.6/522.7/800/540 Hz, duty 0.4798, restarted with their filters on every strike so each hit is the same metal; two band-passes (3440, 7100 Hz) feed three high-passed bands with an envelope each: a long low band, a 7 kHz band with a 30 ms swell, a 40 ms top tick. decay runs from closed hat through open hat to cymbal; tone sets the top tick. It does NOT follow the key: the same metal on every key, never a melodic voice; add a pitched layer with + for a pitch. Linear VCAs (the clipping VCAs are not modelled). No choke between voices; a re-strike on its own voice cuts the ring. It rings only while the synth's voice lives: a long decay needs a long release. Without oversampling the top above 12 kHz is up to 9 dB darker. 1.70 is a level choice.
techniques.code:
kdecay  = 0.40   ; decay[0.0..1.0]: closed hat to long cymbal, one continuum
ktone   = 0.50   ; tone[0..1]: level of the short top band against the two long ones
; DECAY: SELF
; LOUDNESS: decay
; FOLLOWS kfreq: no
; body resonance, FIXED in Hz
; TR-808 cymbal/hat after Werner, Abel & Smith (ICMC-SMC 2014): six Schmitt-trigger
; squares (their measured frequencies and duty), two band-passes, three enveloped bands.
kup timeinsts
if changed2(ktrig) == 1 then
  reinit MET
endif
MET:
; no strike at orchestra build: the section runs once there with kup = 0
iamp = (i(kup) > 0 ? 1.0 : 0)
; band-limited pulses restarted on every strike at fixed phases: each hit the same metal

a2 vco2 1, 304.4, 2, 0.4798, 0.17
a3 vco2 1, 369.6, 2, 0.4798, 0.53
a4 vco2 1, 522.7, 2, 0.4798, 0.71
a5 vco2 1, 800, 2, 0.4798, 0.29
a6 vco2 1, 540, 2, 0.4798, 0.83

idk = 0.15 + i(kdecay)*i(kdecay)*1.85

ae2 expsega 0.001, 0.03, iamp+0.001, idk*0.5, 0.001, 1, 0.001
ae3 expsega 0.001, 0.0003, iamp+0.001, 0.001, iamp+0.001, 0.04, 0.001, 1, 0.001

ab1 butbp amix, 3440, 1000
ab2 butbp amix, 7100, 1500

ah2 buthp ab2*(ae2-0.001), 5000
ah3 buthp ab2*(ae3-0.001), 9000

decay.note: Ring time of the low band, 0.15 s to 2 s on a square law (the 7 kHz band rings half as long): at 0 the hit is gone in about 0.14 s, at 1 it rings about 1.8 s. Read at the strike, so a change applies from the next hit.

closed.gloss: closed hat: the strike and a short metal ring, silent after about 0.14 s

open.gloss: open hat: the metal hangs for under half a second

cymbal.gloss: 808 cymbal: the low metal band rings for nearly two seconds

tone.note: Level of the short top band (above 9 kHz, gone in 40 ms) against the two long bands, from removed (0) to 1.4 (1): the stick's tick in the first 5 ms, about 10 dB above 9 kHz. It leaves the ring as it is.

soft.gloss: the top band removed: the strike without its tick

hard.gloss: the top band's tick pushed to 1.4 of its level

techniques.why: ring modulation / AM at a 2:1 ratio -- carrier f times modulator 2f, so sum and difference land on f and 3f: a hollow ODD-harmonic tone (square-adjacent), with a drifting diode imbalance and carrier leak for the metallic edge
techniques.code:
krmw0   poscil 0.004, 0.091          ; modulator drift, ~7 cents
krlk0   poscil 0.03, 0.037           ; diode imbalance, drifting
acar0   poscil 0.8, (kfreq * koct1)
amod0   poscil 1.0, (kfreq * koct1) * (2.0 + krmw0)
asig    = acar0 * (amod0 * 0.88 + 0.10 + krlk0) ; ring mod + carrier leak

techniques.why: Chebyshev waveshaper -- a fixed transfer table (GEN13) holding odd Chebyshev terms up to the 11th, which map exactly onto odd harmonics: the controlled way to add drive, dirt and distortion colour
techniques.code:
kdrv0   poscil 0.12, 0.074           ; drive wander
kdrb0   poscil 0.05, 0.119           ; second, incommensurate
adrv0   poscil 0.30 + kdrv0 + kdrb0, (kfreq * koct1)
ash0    tablei adrv0, giCheb, 1, 0.5 ; Chebyshev transfer curve
asig    = ash0 * 0.55           ; level-match the family

techniques.why: pipe / drawbar organ -- tonewheel and church organ: three ranks at typical registration, an 8' principal, a 4' octave and a 5 1/3' quint, each its own gbuzz stack, each drifting at its own rate

kw40    poscil 0.00045, 0.083        ; rank 4', incommensurate
kwq0    poscil 0.00030, 0.107        ; quint rank, incommensurate
a80     gbuzz 0.46, (kfreq * koct1) * (1 + kw80), 6, 1, 0.72, giCos ; 8' principal
a40     gbuzz 0.24, (kfreq * koct1) * 2.0023 * (1 + kw40), 4, 1, 0.66, giCos ; 4' octave, +4 cents
aq0     gbuzz 0.16, (kfreq * koct1) * 1.4987 * (1 + kwq0), 3, 1, 0.60, giCos ; 5 1/3' quint, -1.5 cents

techniques.why: clarinet / chalumeau / bass clarinet -- a cylindrical single-reed bore, on the physical model this build ships for exactly that: Csound's `wgclar`, Perry Cook's clarinet in Smith's digital-waveguide formulation (Cook, ICMC 1992; Smith, 'Physical Modeling using Digital Waveguides', CMJ 16(4), 1992). The odd-only series is not an approximation here, it is what a cylinder closed at the reed produces. Replaces an `foscili` pair at modulator ratio 2 that stood in for it: that had 0.00% of its energy above 2 kHz and no even partials at all (-140 dB), a clean odd stack with no air in it whatever, and it carried no knob the player could reach.
techniques.code:
; LOUDNESS: blow
; `blow` is the blowing PRESSURE on this reed and pressure carries level with it --
; a clarinet blown harder is louder, which is the physics and not an invented
; envelope. Every number here is measured at 176400, the rate the plugin compiles
; Csound at, and read after decimation to 44100; a bare-44100 reading of this model
; is a different instrument (same body, centroid 340 Hz there against 1235 Hz here).
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes -- 0 to -11 cents from 55 Hz to 880 Hz, rms flat within 0.21 dB
; across that span, so the chalumeau and the bass register are this same body played
; low. STANDS: it is driven and holds as long as the note does.
; `kngain` IS NOT BREATH NOISE, whatever its name and the manual suggest. BJ heard it
; first and the split confirms it: over this axis the INHARMONIC share moves 0.15% ->
; 0.31% while the HARMONIC energy above 2 kHz goes 2.96% -> 24.81%. What it does is
; feed the reed nonlinearity, which redistributes the odd series upward -- at the low
; end the partials fall away smoothly (3rd..15th: -9.6 -14.1 -16.9 -19.0 -20.8 -22.5
; -24.1 dB), at the high end the upper ones carry the tone (-6.3 -19.7 -9.5 -2.5
; -29.2 -4.9 -12.6). Real noise appears only past `kngain` 0.6, and there the rms has
; collapsed to 0.061 because the model has left self-oscillation. So there is no
; breath in this bore to reach for; a breath layer would have to be MIXED IN, which
; this instrument is entitled to do (BJ 2026-08-05: "das ist ein synth, also kann man
; rauschen zumischen lassen, auch im rezept") and which v1.0 does not yet do.
; THE TWO AXES ARE COUPLED IN THE MODEL and the ranges are picked so each still
; travels on its own. Below `kngain` 0.20 nothing at all comes up, and the pressure
; at which the reed opens falls as `kngain` rises: kamp 0.83 at kngain 0.25, 0.70 at
; 0.35, 0.45 at 0.50.
; THE MOVEMENT IS THE BREATH, not a wobble laid on the pitch: a slow unsteadiness in
; the blowing pressure, which is what a player's breath does. It is small (0.02 of
; the pressure) and it stays inside the turbulent regime at every position of both
; knobs, because crossing that boundary inside a note is what an earlier, wider
; version did and it cost 58 dB of loudness travel in one note.
; NO ATTACK IS WRITTEN HERE and none can be. `wgclar`'s own `iatt` is dead in this
; host: one instance per voice is started at engine build and never restarted, so a
; note only unmutes a bore that is already standing -- measured with a preroll, 0.99
; of full level 5 ms after the gate opens, and IDENTICAL for a pressure ramp of
; 0.02 s and one of 0.24 s. A ramp changes only where the bore settles afterwards
; (hysteresis), which is a side effect and not an onset. The player's envelope owns
; the attack.
kovertone = 0.55   ; overtone [0.00..1.00]: how far up the reed is worked -- from a hollow chalumeau on its lowest partials to a bright reedy tone standing on its upper ones
kblow   = 0.55   ; blow [0.00..1.00]: how hard the reed is blown -- the pressure on the bore, soft and pure to driven and turbulent
kng     = 0.30 + 0.20 * kovertone                ; 0.50 is the ceiling: past it the model leaves
                                             ; self-oscillation entirely (rms 0.062 at 0.7).
                                             ; 0.30 is the dry end -- below 0.20 no pressure
                                             ; whatever brings breath out of the bore.
kwander oscili 0.02, 0.23, giSine            ; a player's breath is never quite steady
kpr     = 0.55 + 0.35 * kblow + kwander               ; started below the turbulent boundary a note stays
                                             ; dull for its whole length (hysteresis, measured:
                                             ; floor 0.35 -> 2.9% above 2 kHz where floor 0.45 ->
                                             ; 18.0% at the same target), so the range begins above it.
asig    wgclar kpr, kfreq * koct1, -0.3, 0.1, 0.1, kng, 5.735, 0, giSine, 30
                                             ; the -0.3 is `kstiff`, INERT in this build (output
                                             ; bit-identical -0.9 to 0.0 at both rates), so it sits at
                                             ; the documented value and never moves. kvamp is 0: no
                                             ; built-in vibrato. ONE wgclar and no more -- a second
                                             ; instance changes this one, 3rd partial -5.9 -> -14.1 dB.
asig    = asig * 1.30 * kvol1

overtone.note: how far up the reed is worked -- `kngain` over 0.30..0.50. NOT breath noise, whatever the argument's name suggests: measured at 176400 and read after decimation to 44100, the inharmonic share moves only 0.15% -> 0.31% across this axis while the harmonic energy above 2 kHz goes 2.96% -> 24.81%. It feeds the reed nonlinearity and the odd series redistributes upward -- 3rd to 15th partial -9.6 -14.1 -16.9 -19.0 -20.8 -22.5 -24.1 dB at the low end against -6.3 -19.7 -9.5 -2.5 -29.2 -4.9 -12.6 at the high one, so it is a change of which partials carry the tone and not a tilt. 0.50 is a hard ceiling: real noise only appears past 0.6 and by then the model has left self-oscillation (rms 0.061 at 0.7). COUPLED TO `blow`: the pressure at which the reed opens falls as this rises -- kamp 0.83 at kngain 0.25, 0.70 at 0.35, 0.45 at 0.50.

hollow.gloss: the chalumeau, standing on its lowest partials

open.gloss: the upper odd partials coming up under the tone

reedy.gloss: bright, the tone carried by its upper partials

blow.note: how hard the reed is blown -- `kamp` over 0.50..0.90, which on this model is the blowing PRESSURE and not an output level. Measured at 176400 and read after decimation to 44100, at the authored `air`: the rms rises 0.21 -> 0.47 (7.2 dB) while the energy above 2 kHz goes 2.9% -> 35.3% and the centroid 446 -> 2046 Hz, so colour travels with the level rather than instead of it -- declared `; LOUDNESS: blow`, because a clarinet blown harder IS louder. Do not read the older 44100 figures for this argument: at a bare 44100 it shows a threshold at 0.76 that does not exist at the rate the plugin runs. The range stops at 0.90 because the model keeps rising past it with nothing new in the tone, and starts at 0.50 because a note begun below the turbulent boundary stays dull for its whole length (hysteresis, measured: floor 0.35 -> 2.9% above 2 kHz where floor 0.45 -> 18.0%, same target pressure).

soft.gloss: pure and contained, the reed barely worked

spoken.gloss: the normal weight of the tone

driven.gloss: pushed until the reed turns turbulent

techniques.why: plucked string / guitar / harp / koto / pizzicato (a violin or cello PLUCKED): ONE real string, set going and then left to ring -- NOT the ensemble string machine (that is `strings`, detuned saws) and NOT the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (that is `harpsichord`, gbuzz choirs). The string is a comb resonator tuned to the played pitch. It has to be fed the whole time so a held note stands and the synth's own envelope does the striking -- but the feed arrives as scattered, time-smeared touches and the ring is kept long, so what is heard is the string and not what is driving it. A continuous wall of noise into the same resonator is audibly an electric string driver: aggressive and restless. Its top dies away after the attack the way a real string loses its brilliance -- twice over, fast for the first instant and slowly for the whole ring. IF THE PROMPT WANTS A PLUCK THAT IS ALLOWED TO DIE -- struck once and left to ring down under the key -- this entry cannot do it, because it is fed the whole time on purpose; `plucked_wire` is the one, a real Karplus-Strong wire with nothing driving it after the pluck. Choose between them from what the prompt asks for. bow = plucked with a pick to drawn with a bow, pick = where the string is set going, from right at the bridge to at the middle, damp = left ringing to stopped under the hand A STRING DRAWN WITH A BOW -- violin, viola, cello, bass, arco -- is `bowed_string`: a real bow on a waveguide string. This entry's `bow` axis only thickens the dust that drives the resonator, and BJ never took it.
techniques.code:
kdamp   = 0.00   ; damp [0.00..1.00]: the flat of the hand on the string, from left ringing to stopped
kpick   = 0.185  ; pick [0.10..0.50]: where along the string it is set going, as a fraction of its length
kstr    limit kfreq * koct1, 20, 12000
kfast   = exp(-knote * 20.00)                  ; the first instant's brilliance goes at once
kslow   = exp(-knote * 0.328)                  ; and the string keeps losing its top all the while
kbrth   poscil 0.120, 1.900                ; the hand behind it is never quite steady
kcut    limit 775.0 * (1 + 2.58 * kfast) * (1 + 4.06 * kslow) * (1 + kbrth) * (1 - 0.85 * kdamp), 60, 18000
aexd    dust 1.0, 736.2                        ; the drive arrives as separate touches, not as
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.1100, 0.00710                ;   a wall of noise -- a wall is an electric
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0820, 0.00470                ;   string driver, not a played string. Each
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0640, 0.00310                ;   touch is then smeared out in time so none
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0480, 0.00190                ;   of them arrives as a click. Allpasses
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0340, 0.00113                ;   spread WITHOUT darkening; a lowpass here
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0260, 0.00079                ;   buries the instrument's own colour
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0200, 0.00053
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0160, 0.00037
aexb    tone aexd, kcut
apik    vdelay aexb, (kpick / kstr) * 1000, 60
aexc    = aexb - apik
astr    streson aexc, kstr, 0.9884
aref    poscil 0.35, 400                          ; a fixed-loudness yardstick: how scattered the
abal    balance astr, aref                        ; drive is must not change how loud the tone is
asig    = abal * 0.85

bow.note: how the string is set going, and that is the whole difference between a guitar and a cello. A pick or a fingernail lets go in an instant, so everything in the string is woken at once and the sound arrives bright and then falls away. A bow never lets go: the hair grabs and slips and grabs again, feeding the string the whole time, so the top is rubbed off but nothing dies -- the tone stands and breathes instead. In the code this is how DENSELY the drive arrives: separate touches at the plucked end, a steady draw at the bowed one. Measured across the axis the colour travels from 4812 Hz down to 3463 Hz while how sharply the string rings does not change (34.3 -> 33.6 dB) and the loudness moves 0.04 dB.

plucked.gloss: picked and let go: bright at the front, then darkening

bowed.gloss: drawn with a bow: standing, breathing, the top rubbed off

pick.note: where along the string it is set going, as a fraction of its length. Not a tone control -- geometry: the body subtracts a copy of the drive delayed by `pick` of a period, so the harmonic whose node falls on that spot cannot be given any energy and is simply missing. That harmonic is 1/pick, so the axis is a NOTCH WALKING DOWN through the harmonics as it rises, and it bites hardest where 1/pick lands on one. Measured at 220 Hz, how far that harmonic sits below its neighbours: 0.10 takes 39 dB out of the 10th, 0.125 36 dB out of the 8th, 0.167 34 dB out of the 6th, 0.20 41 dB out of the 5th, 0.25 46 dB out of the 4th, 0.333 42 dB out of the 3rd, and 0.50 cancels EVERY even harmonic at once (44 dB, odd-to-even 44.1 dB) -- the hollow, woody one. BETWEEN those positions the notch falls between two harmonics and does much less: at the shipped default 0.185 the null sits at 5.4, BETWEEN two harmonics, so no harmonic is cancelled at all -- the fifth reads 1.8 to 10.0 dB below its neighbours depending on register (the comb's closed form 2|sin(pi n beta)| gives 6.6 dB; the spread is the broadband drive scattering the partial readings, not the axis), against the 34 to 46 dB above where the null lands ON one. That is why that one setting sounds like no setting at all. The default is 0.185 because that is what the entry has always played; if the sound wants its pluck position HEARD, start it at 0.25, 0.333 or 0.50. Loudness across the whole axis and four registers: 0.035 dB.

wiry.gloss: close to the bridge: the tenth harmonic cancelled, thin and hard

hollow.gloss: a quarter along: the fourth harmonic gone, 46 dB down

middle.gloss: over the middle: EVERY even harmonic gone at once, hollow and woody -- a clarinet made of string

damp.note: how freely the string is allowed to ring, as with the flat of the hand laid on it. Damping a string is a FREQUENCY-DEPENDENT loss and nothing else: the hand takes the highs first and the low partials keep going, which is why a muted string reads as dull rather than as quiet. In a digital string that loss is the loop filter (Jaffe & Smith, CMJ 7(2) 1983). `streson` exposes no loop filter, so THIS AXIS IS NOT ONE: it is the cutoff of the `tone` standing in FRONT of the resonator, scaled by `1 - 0.85 * kdamp`, and the difference is measurable and must be known before choosing a setting. A loop filter applies its loss once per round trip, so the loss compounds; a one-pole on the drive applies it once, and once its cutoff is below the played fundamental the RATIO between partial n and partial 1 stops changing. The axis therefore SATURATES, and how much of it is left depends on the register. Centroid travel over the whole axis, measured at the 4x the LRO runs: 1.55 octaves at 55 Hz, 1.58 at 110, 1.38 at 220, 1.05 at 440, 0.48 at 880 and 0.26 at 1760 (at 44100 it is 1.29 / 1.20 / 0.91 / 0.65 / 0.41 / 0.21). USE IT BELOW ABOUT 440 Hz. Above C5 it is worth less than this entry's own `bow`, which BJ heard as barely audible at 0.77 octaves. It is also back-loaded: at 220 Hz the four quarters give 0.18 / 0.25 / 0.36 / 0.59 octaves, so the last quarter is over 40 % of the whole travel and the `damped` anchor at 0.5 sits at less than a third of it. SECOND EFFECT, declare it rather than discover it: the scaling multiplies the whole `kcut` product, note envelopes included, so damping also softens this body's attack colour instead of sharpening it the way a real loop filter would -- the ratio of the first 50 ms centroid to the sustained one falls from 3.73x to 2.19x at 880 Hz and 2.87x to 1.87x at 440. `streson`'s own feedback is NOT touched and must not be: it is one flat gain for every partial, so lowering it does not damp anything -- it removes the resonance and leaves the broadband drive, which the closing `balance` then amplifies. That is what this axis used to do, and it is worth writing down because a comb-contrast meter certified it: balance had to apply 3.7x at 0 and 15.8x at 1, and the centroid ROSE 3099 -> 4924 Hz. Brighter and noisier, i.e. the opposite. Loudness over the whole damp x pick grid at six registers and both rates: 0.09 dB; true peaks 0.65 to 1.05 against the host's 2.523. THE SHIPPED STRING IS THE OPEN ONE, so the default is 0 and the axis only ever damps.

open.gloss: left to ring: the full top of the string, a clear singing note

damped.gloss: a hand resting on it: the top rolled off, the note dulls but is still a note -- and this is under a third of the travel, not half of it

muted.gloss: palm-muted: dark and dull in the low and middle registers, the highs gone and the low partials still ringing. Above C5 the axis has little left to take

params.bow: nur sehr schwach -- gemessen 0,77 Oktaven Helligkeit zwischen den drei Ankern, und angeregt wird an allen dreien mit `dust`. UNVERÄNDERT gelassen (BJ 2026-08-02: nur damp und pick)
params.pick: kein Unterschied -- gemessen: beim ausgelieferten 0.185 liegt die Kerbe ZWISCHEN dem 5. und 6. Teilton, also wird gar kein Teilton ausgelöscht (1,8 bis 10,0 dB je nach Lage, geschlossene Form 6,6 dB -- gegenüber 34 bis 46 dB dort, wo die Kerbe auf einem Teilton sitzt). Die Achse steht jetzt als Code im Körper, Bereich 0.10..0.50
params.damp: zweimal falsch verdrahtet gewesen. Erst gar kein Code (der Autor erfand die Zeile), dann `streson`s Rückkopplung -- die ist flach über alle Teiltöne, senkt man sie, verschwindet die Resonanz und `balance` hebt den rohen Breitband-Antrieb an: Centroid 3099 -> 4924 Hz statt herunter. Genau BJs Höreindruck. Jetzt die Grenzfrequenz des Filters VOR dem Resonator -- ausdrücklich NICHT in der Schleife, die gibt `streson` nicht her, und deshalb sättigt die Achse: 1,58 Oktaven Reiseweg bei 110 Hz, aber nur 0,48 bei 880 und 0,26 bei 1760. Unterhalb C5 brauchbar, darüber weniger als `bow`, das BJ schon kaum gehört hat. Gehört und von BJ als verifiziert akzeptiert, ausdrücklich noch beta und nicht abgenommen.
